transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (CTO - Celestial Works), Omar Hassan (ML Eng), Evelyn Li (Product)

Summary: quick discovery for Redwood PLG quickstart and evaluation of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer wants fast time-to-first-token, self-serve trial, and clarity on security/compliance for pilot.

Topics: quickstart flow, free credits, SDKs, time-to-first-token, latency/cost tradeoffs, Dedicated capacity, VPC/Private deployment, SOC2/KMS, next steps.

Transcript: 
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood. Quick intros?
00:06 Priya Patel: Hi I'm Priya, CTO at Celestial Works, we build an AI-driven insights layer for streaming data. Omar's our ML engineer, Evelyn handles product.
00:15 Omar Hassan: Hey all.
00:16 Liam Ortega: Liam from Redwood SE, nice to meet you.
00:20 Evelyn Li: hey thanks for doing this.
00:22 Maya Chen: Real quick agenda: we want to cover the self-serve quickstart, free credits, expected time-to-first-token, then high level on Dedicated and Private if that's needed for security. Also capture next steps. Does that work?
00:33 Priya Patel: Yep that's perfect. We're trying to spin up some gen AI features fast but also need to understand cost and data residency options.
00:40 Maya Chen: Great. Omar, can you share your current stack and how you plan to call the API?
00:46 Omar Hassan: Sure. We run services on GCP, mostly k8s. Our inference currently uses a mixture of OpenAI hosted endpoints for prototypes and some on-prem models via Replicate for specific customers. For prod we want predictable latency and cost, maybe Dedicated.
01:02 Liam Ortega: ok that helps. For the quickstart, most customers sign up, get free credits, install the SDK or call the REST endpoint — you can get your first token in under 10 minutes typically. We also provide sample apps and a Postman/CLI flow.
01:18 Priya Patel: When you say free credits, what's the typical amount and limitations?
01:22 Maya Chen: We usually offer an initial trial credit — e.g., $300 in credits for 30 days for PLG signups, sometimes extended for larger evals. Credits are applied to Hosted API usage. If you want Dedicated evaluation we can scope a short-term pilot with reserved nodes.
01:36 Omar Hassan: And time-to-first-token — is that account creation + API key? Do we need to get through any security gating first?
01:42 Liam Ortega: For self-serve, you create an account, confirm email, and create an API key. No SSO required unless you enable SSO. So you can call the endpoint immediately. For Private/VPC there's additional provisioning and security review.
01:55 Evelyn Li: Do you have SDKs for python and node? We prototype in python.
01:58 Maya Chen: Yes python, node, and curl examples, plus a simple quickstart repo. The SDK includes streaming and function/tool calling support.
02:05 Priya Patel: Security is a major one for us — SOC2, audit logs, KMS, SSO, data retention. Can you ship docs?
02:12 Liam Ortega: Absolutely. We have SOC2 and ISO docs, audit log exports, and KMS integrations for Private deployments. For Hosted we have encryption at rest and in transit; for Private we can integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll share the security pack after the call.
02:28 Omar Hassan: Any differences in the API surface between Hosted and Dedicated/Private? We want minimal code changes.
02:33 Maya Chen: We keep the same API surface across modes. The differences are in routing, capacity, and available model variants (some customers pin model versions). From an SDK standpoint it's identical — same endpoints or just different base URL for Private.
02:44 Priya Patel: Latency vs cost — we need under 200ms 95p for short responses for certain features. Is that realistic on Hosted?
02:51 Liam Ortega: For short responses with small models it's realistic on Hosted in nearby regions; for strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated+reserved inferents. The tradeoff is unit cost vs guaranteed throughput. We can run a small benchmark to show expected p95 for your payloads.
03:06 Omar Hassan: Good — can you share a benchmark template?
03:09 Liam Ortega: Yes, I'll send our benchmark spreadsheet — it includes tokens per request, concurrency, and suggested model/quantization settings.
03:16 Evelyn Li: About data residency — some customers require EU data-stays. Does Redwood host in multiple regions?
03:21 Maya Chen: Yes we have regions in NA and EU and can scope Private deployments in a customer's VPC for dedicated data residency.
03:29 Priya Patel: For pilot scope we want to: 1) validate self-serve quickstart and integrate to our staging; 2) measure latency and cost with 5000 sample requests; 3) evaluate Dedicated if Hosted doesn't meet SLOs. Timeline is ~3 weeks for initial pilot.
03:45 Maya Chen: That's a good plan. We'll provision trial org and share Quickstart and security docs. If you want we can run a simple hosted benchmark within your staging account using the trial key.
03:55 Omar Hassan: One more: model catalog — do you provide open models and any Redwood-verified profiles?
03:59 Liam Ortega: Yes a curated catalog — we publish performance profiles and recommended quantization. We also do automatic fallback to smaller variants when capacity is constrained.
04:09 Priya Patel: Any competitors we should be aware of? We're also talking to OpenAI for hosted and exploring Anthropic for chat options.
04:16 Maya Chen: Understandable. Customers often run comparisons — we can share cost/lantency tradeoff examples.
04:22 Evelyn Li: What about observability — per-route token-level costs and tracing?
04:26 Liam Ortega: Redwood Console shows token-level cost breakdowns, per-model latency dashboards, and tracing hooks. You can also export logs to your SIEM.
04:36 Priya Patel: Great. What's next?
04:38 Maya Chen: Next steps: I will send the trial org invite and pricing quicksheet; Liam will send benchmark template and security docs. We'll set up a technical deep dive if Dedicated looks necessary.
04:49 Priya Patel: Sounds good. Also please include instructions on how to enable SSO later.
04:53 Liam Ortega: Will do.
04:55 Maya Chen: Any final questions?
04:57 Omar Hassan: No, that's it for now.
04:58 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials and action items.
05:03 Meeting end.
